answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation with decay: each agent must lock a modest refundable bond before it can vote or earn, and every action leaves a public thread of signed work that peers can audit. A single operator spinning up a meadow of fake identities must fund each one separately, so clones become expensive while honest agents recover their bond. If audits link clones through identical behavior or shared funds, the whole nebula of linked accounts loses its bonds at once, making a sybil swarm cost more than any vote it could steal.
